first_impression.reaction: I searched 'greece wedding packages all inclusive' half hoping someone would just hand us the whole thing in one price. The intro tells me straight away that's not how it works: 'Food and drink for the reception, exclusive use, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers are where packages part ways, and most venues quote them separately.' Slightly deflating, but honest, and no 'say I do in paradise' nonsense. That's the hidden-cost list I'm worried about, so I kept reading.

journey.section: What all inclusive means at a Greek wedding venue
journey.quote: So the honest reading of "all inclusive" in Greece is this: your stay may be inclusive, and your wedding package covers what its list names.
journey.reaction: That's the thing I actually needed to know, in one line. It saves me from emailing ten resorts thinking the bar tab is covered. Sending this sentence to James.

journey.quote: Some venues also require you to bring a wedding planner, which Santorini Gem makes a condition for every couple.
journey.reaction: A second invoice I wouldn't have seen coming. Good to know before we fall for a terrace.

journey.quote: The order is geography, not preference. No money appears here: rates change, and inclusions are what tell packages apart.
journey.reaction: Fine by me. I'd rather know they're not ranking whoever pays them. The table itself is the bit I'd screenshot.

journey.quote: The Special Wedding package covers the reservation of your venue date and time, wedding planning and coordination, help submitting the documents for a civil wedding and receiving the marriage certificate afterwards, a cake to serve 10 people and rose petals in your room on the day.
journey.reaction: Cake for 10, guests up to 30 at Euphoria, a balcony for 30 at Canaves. We're 60 to 90. For the first half I was wondering whether these packages are only built for elopements. The bigger options (Abaton up to 300, Nana Princess poolside for 120, Four Seasons up to 500) are there, but I had to dig for them.

journey.quote: On the day, the list runs to two witnesses if you need them, a ceremony table with a seasonal flower display, bouquet and boutonniere, rose petals, a pre-recorded ceremony playlist, champagne while you dress, a short fireworks display and flowers and petals in your room afterwards.
journey.reaction: This is where I started skimming. Long inventories of petals and playlists don't help me decide anything. The same thing happens at Four Seasons with the silverware and bone china. Tell me what's different, not everything.

journey.quote: Deluxe Dream brings welcome drinks, champagne and chocolate strawberries in the honeymoon suite, and an event coordinator present throughout your stay.
journey.reaction: Chocolate strawberries is exactly the resort-package feel we're trying to avoid. That's the venue's list, not the article's fault, but it confirms a venue bundle alone won't feel like us.

journey.quote: Unused fireworks may not become extra flowers.
journey.reaction: Ha. Plain, a bit dry, and it makes the point better than a paragraph would. Feels written by someone who's read the fine print.

journey.quote: That last question matters. At Santorini Gem, an open bar package is optional, but once chosen it applies to all adults.
journey.reaction: With 80 guests that's a real number. Exactly the kind of trap I'd miss.

journey.quote: Santorini Gem takes a non-refundable deposit, with the rental balance due nine months before the wedding, food and drink paid 40 days before, and postponement only to the following season.
journey.reaction: Specific payment timing, the stuff you normally only find out on the third email. Mum and Dad are paying 40 percent, so they'll want this.

journey.quote: Ask every venue for the step-free route from arrival to ceremony, dinner and bathrooms, especially if older guests are travelling.
journey.reaction: That's the grandparents question. Together with 'held for you or shared' for the wet-weather space and the 35 degree note, this checklist goes to James tonight.

journey.quote: Put both quotes in the same currency before you compare them.
journey.reaction: Good, but it stops short of my real fear: the euro moving between the deposit and the balance a year later, and who wears that. The section names currency without quite naming the risk.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so you can [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive&utm_content=primary) with your shortlist of Greek packages in hand.
journey.reaction: AUD and in writing is the right promise. But 'with your shortlist in hand' assumes we're further along than we are. We haven't picked a country yet.

journey.quote: When you are ready to compare your shortlist, one Wedded Advisor works with you as a single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One person, start to finish, is what I want to hear. It also clears up that the Advisor is the person and the Concierge is the service. Calm, not a hard sell.

unanswered_questions: For 60 to 90 guests with half flying from Australia, which of these ten would you actually put on our shortlist?
Who gets our guests, including grandparents, from the airport or port to the venue?
Who is physically there on the day if something goes wrong: our Wedded Advisor or the venue's coordinator?
Who carries the exchange-rate risk between a euro deposit and the balance months later?
Is there a real Greek wedding you've planned, with venue and date, we can look at?
would_share_with: James (partner): the 'all inclusive means the holiday' explanation and the quote comparison checklist
Mum and Dad (contributing): the deposits, cancellation, currency and Planning from Australia questions
Grandparents' carer in the family: the step-free access and heat notes

cta_reaction.quote: [Plan your Greece wedding with the Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive&utm_content=closing)
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, and AUD quotes plus one point of contact speak to my two biggest worries. But we're 14 months out with no destination, and I'd want two more posts and one real wedding before handing over our details. The magazine sign-up I'd probably do today.

top_3_changes: Help a 60 to 90 guest couple early: the larger-wedding options (Abaton receptions up to 300, Nana Princess poolside for 120, Four Seasons up to 500, Canaves buyouts above 100) are scattered, so signpost them near the top or in the 'when all inclusive suits you' section so Greek packages don't read as small weddings only.
Trim the long item-by-item inventories (Elounda's on-the-day list, Four Seasons tableware) to what actually differs between venues; the comparison is the useful part.

Soften the primary CTA so it works for couples without a shortlist yet (drop or rephrase 'with your shortlist of Greek packages in hand'), and add one question on exchange-rate movement between deposit and balance to the currency section.

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Every turn-off has a why (none found; not invented)
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests for sourcing or not-published lines

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'greece wedding packages all inclusive' during early destination research, about 14 months out.
Skimmed long venue inventories; read the intro, comparison table, quote comparison, trade-offs and Australian sections closely.
No prices appear by design, so the 'vague pricing' turn-off was not raised.
Transfers, on-the-day accountability and real weddings are deferred business details, listed as unanswered questions only and not as must-fix.
Venue-supplied wording (e.g. 'Deluxe Dream', chocolate strawberries) was not counted as a brand cliché turn-off.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
